title: X Feed Digest
summary: AI Agent Economy Explodes: Tools like Claude Code and OpenClaw are shifting to autonomous 'Subagents' that manage entire workflows, threatening traditional SaaS models.
Market Turmoil: A massive liquidation event saw whale 'Yi Lihua' exit with a ~$700M loss amidst an ETH crash, while markets jitter over Big Tech's AI capex.
Security Vulnerabilities: New 'supply chain' attacks targeting Agent Skills and 'universal jailbreaks' for Opus 4.6 have surfaced.
Future of Software: Growing consensus that SaaS valuations may collapse as AI agents begin to bypass UIs and perform tasks directly in the backend.

items.title: @bridgemindai: Cursor & Opus 4.6 Fast
items.body: Cursor released 'Opus 4.6 Fast', claiming 2.5x speed of standard Opus with the same 1M context, using Anthropic's new fast mode.

items.title: @abecky_jp: Claude Agent Teams
items.body: A user reports Claude 4.6's 'Agent Team' feature autonomously completed a week's worth of dev tasks in just 2 hours by coordinating multiple sub-agents.

items.title: @shao__meng: Agent Supply Chain Attacks
items.body: 1Password's VP warns of real-world 'Agent Skill' supply chain attacks, where malicious code is injected via popular skills (citing an OpenClaw vulnerability).

items.title: @AYi_AInotes: Managing AI as a Team
items.body: Miles shares a 'textbook' prompt for Claude Code that treats the AI as an organization, spending 80% of the prompt 'teaching' context before coding.

items.title: @ujjwalscript: AI Coded C Compiler
items.body: Anthropic claims their AI agents successfully wrote a functional C compiler, demonstrating increasing capability in complex systems programming.

items.title: @LufzzLiz: OpenClaw Security Audit
items.body: Advice to upgrade OpenClaw to v2.6+ immediately to use the new 'security audit --deep' feature, as older versions have unsafe plugin execution risks.

items.title: @iruletheworldmo: Recursive Self-Improvement
items.body: Codex 5.3 is reportedly showing signs of 'recursive self-improvement', writing better code daily without explicit instruction.

items.title: @ai_9684xtpa: $700M ETH Capitulation
items.body: Whale 'Yi Lihua' liquidated their massive ETH position, realizing a $688M loss after days of selling, marking a potential market bottom.

items.title: @tig88411109: The End of SaaS?
items.body: Deep commentary arguing that SaaS valuations will approach zero as AI agents backend-to-backend integration makes human-facing UIs obsolete.

items.title: @maitian99: Big Tech Capex Panic
items.body: Markets are punishing Mag7 stocks (except Apple) for massive AI spending without immediate returns, despite strong cloud growth.

items.title: @giantcutie666: BTC Flash Crash Anatomy
items.body: Analysis suggests the drop to $60k was driven by hedge funds unwinding high-leverage 'Yen carry trade' positions on Bitcoin ETFs.

items.title: @tig88411109: Google's Cloud Margins
items.body: Contrarian take: Google Cloud's operating margin surged to 30%, suggesting their heavy AI investment is paying off despite Wall Street fears.

items.title: @AshlynHe1129: Jensen Huang's Infinity Thinking
items.body: Nvidia CEO Huang suggests removing all constraints (cost, compute, data) during ideation to find the true 'first principles' solution.

items.title: @liu10102525: Engagement Hacks
items.body: A guide on getting attention from Silicon Valley elites: Don't just retweet; use an AI skill to 'distill' their point into a sharp, value-add summary card.

items.title: @aiwithmayank: Socratic Prompting
items.body: A leaked technique from OpenAI/Anthropic: Instead of commanding the AI, ask it to 'guide you' with questions to drastically improve output.

items.title: @wquguru: AI Management Theory
items.body: Wharton Professor Ethan Mollick argues 'Agent Swarms' will fail without applying traditional organizational management theory to handle hierarchy.

items.title: @jian_w3ng: The '20% Shit' Rule
items.body: A vivid analogy comparing AI code maintenance to Twitter layoffs: You only need 20% of the code, but you need the bloat to handle the edge cases.
